# Terra & Form

> Architecture and interior design studio based in Bangkok, Thailand. Trilingual website (French / English / Thai).

Terra & Form designs new-build residences, renovations and extensions, interiors, commercial fit-outs and brand identities in Bangkok, with a contextual approach where site, climate and materials always come before form. Every project follows four stages: framing (site, brief, budget, timeline), design (spatial and material direction), development (drawings, details, visualisations) and delivery (coordination through to handover).

- [Studio](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/studio/): The studio's practice, principles and past projects.
- [Services](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/services/): New-build residential, renovation/extension, interiors, commercial and brand identity work.
- [Journal](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/journal/): Articles on architecture trends -- regenerative design, mass timber, tropical modernism, floating and resilient architecture.
- [FAQ](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/faq/): Answers on project types, service area, process, timelines, budget, permits and contact.

## Projects (EN)

- [Skyline Residence](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/projet/residence-bangkok/): A residence conceived as a vantage point over the city, its wide glazed openings framing the Bangkok skyline from every room.
- [Ladprao Villa](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/projet/villa-ladprao/): Contemporary villa with pool, clean white volumes softened by timber joinery.
- [Phrom Phong Villa](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/projet/villa-phromphong/): Entrance framed by timber screens and a dense tropical garden, for an intimate arrival despite the urban setting.

## Journal articles (EN)

- [Wellness Architecture and Biophilic Design](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/article/architecture-bien-etre-biophilique/): Living walls, organic forms, low-carbon materials: how biophilic design is reshaping the way spaces are conceived for their occupants' physical and mental health.
- [Regenerative Architecture](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/article/architecture-regenerative/): Biodiversity corridors, pollinator-friendly facades, ecosystem restoration: when buildings stop doing harm and start repairing.
- [Resilient and Floating Architecture](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/article/architecture-resiliente-flottante/): Amphibious structures, floating neighbourhoods, corrosion-resistant materials: how Bangkok is becoming a global laboratory for architecture facing rising waters.
- [Architecture and Food Security](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/article/architecture-securite-alimentaire/): Hydroponics, aeroponics, building-integrated vertical farms: how architecture is becoming an active player in urban food security, neighbourhood by neighbourhood.
- [Underground Architecture: The New Inverted Verticality](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/article/architecture-souterraine-verticalite-inversee/): Thermal mass, fiber-optic heliostats, flood-smart urbanism: how Bangkok is reinventing depth to escape the heat and urban saturation.
- [3D Printing and Construction Robotics](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/article/impression-3d-robotique-chantier/): Layer-by-layer printed concrete, robotic bricklayers, technological conductor: how automation is reshaping the architect's role without replacing it.
- [High-Tech Timber Architecture (Mass Timber)](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/article/mass-timber-architecture/): CLT, glulam, carbon sequestration: how structural timber is redrawing skyscrapers and turning cities into carbon sinks.
- [Thailand: When Tradition Meets Tropical Modernism](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/article/tradition-modernisme-tropical/): Stilts, deep roof overhangs, bamboo and raw concrete: how a new generation of Thai practices is reinventing vernacular housing to meet climate and Bangkok's urban density.
- [Vernacular 2.0: Reinventing Ancestral Knowledge](https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/article/vernaculaire-2-0/): Thermal simulation, augmented local materials, artisanal know-how: how the algorithm is bringing ancestral building techniques back into fashion.
